key_insight: Autocata turns catalyst discovery into an autonomous, language-driven workflow by mapping reaction-network goals to reusable generative and evaluation capabilities.
engineering_relevance: This enables scalable catalyst screening with less human orchestration, helping researchers explore complex multi-step reaction pathways across multiple chemistries more efficiently.
method: Uses a capability registry of 79 adsorbate-specialized generative models covering C/N/O/H reaction intermediates.
Starts from a natural-language prompt, decomposes the reaction network, configures the right models, and generates candidate surface structures.
Filters candidates for physical/geometric validity and ranks them with machine-learning potential evaluations, adapting workflows when bottlenecks arise.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a Transformer pretrained on two million catalyst-adsorbate structures and demonstrations on CH4 activation, N2RR, and CO2-to-methanol pathways.
watch_item: Performance likely depends on the completeness of the capability registry and the reliability of validity filtering and ML-potential ranking for unfamiliar reaction spaces.
paper_title: Autocata: Reaction-network-guided autonomous catalyst screening via capability-centric AI
